job: GitHub Actions scheduled data-bake: refresh free-tier data as committed JSON, no server (plan C5 step 1; founder decision D-2026-08-12-free-tier).
context: The site is fully static. Data that changes over time (cost indexes from StatCan 18-10-0276-01, open Alberta land datasets, listing-metadata expiry lint, the HOMES mint verification) should refresh on a schedule by committing JSON - never by adding a runtime backend.
rejectionGates: the workflow must be enabled by the FOUNDER (it needs Actions write permission and creates commits) - prepare it fully, open a PR or leave it on a branch, and say so in the evidence
no paid APIs, no scraping restricted sources, no partner outreach (D-2026-08-12-free-tier)
bake commits must be as the github-actions bot with a fixed message prefix 'bake:' so release provenance stays legible
instructions: 1. Write .github/workflows/data-bake.yml: cron weekly (e.g. Mondays 12:00 UTC) + workflow_dispatch; checkout, node 20, run each bake script, git diff --quiet || commit + push. Do NOT auto-deploy - the deploy stays a human-triggered release.

2. First bake script: app/scripts/bake-mint-verification.mjs already effectively exists as scripts/verify-homes-mint.mjs - call it and commit data/homes/mint-verification.json when the block advances.

3. DONE (C2, Aug 14) but NOT with the table this manifest named: 18-10-0276-01 is ARCHIVED, its last reference period is 2024-04-01, and StatCan's own footnote says it was replaced when 2024 Q2 shipped. Baking the named table would have published a two-year-stale index under a fresh retrieval date - the exact quiet falsehood this node exists to prevent. app/scripts/bake-cost-indexes.mjs bakes the live successor 18-10-0289-01 to data/cost-indexes/statcan-1810028901.json (25 regions x 14 divisions), carries supersedes + StatCan's footnote in the artifact, and REFUSES TO RUN if its table ever stops being CURRENT. Add `node app/scripts/bake-cost-indexes.mjs` as a workflow step.
4. Third: a lint step that fails the workflow when any licensed-photo permission in data/listings (once C-1 lands) is past expiresAtISO.
5. Evidence: the workflow file, one successful local dry-run of each script, and a note that enabling the schedule is a founder action.

verify.note: plus actionlint or GitHub's workflow parser via a draft PR

sideEffect: local (remote-write only when the founder enables the schedule)

evidence.delivered: .github/workflows/data-bake.yml (workflow_dispatch + Monday cron; runs verify-homes-mint.mjs and commits data/ changes as the actions bot with the 'bake:' prefix; deploys stay human-triggered). The mint script's local dry-run is recorded in VT03. Cost-index and photo-expiry bake steps remain for C-1/C-2 when their data lands - the workflow grows a step per bake script.
